prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, hip-cut demi statue portrait, an irregular asymmetric-panelled multi-material body, every material seam physically stepped. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to two individually finished thigh-stub tips just below her hip line, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her form comes to an end, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Italian woman in 1960s Italian film-star makeup — warm olive skin, thick strongly arched dark brows, a long black liner winging up and out at the outer corner of each eye, soft brown eyeshadow, long lashes, large dark eyes with bright real catchlights, a deep red lip with a defined edge, thick glossy dark-brown hair set in a high backcombed style, a smouldering, confident expression. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. On each ear a large real pearl drop with a gold clip.

Physique: A colossal heavy chest wider than her shoulders, a waistline that still pulls in sharply, then an enormous belly and colossal wide hips flaring out again, her body four irregular panels of crystal, stone, glass-vessel and wood, each panel physically stepped from its neighbours.

Boundary (skin to material, at the collarbones): a single straight, flat line runs around the base of her neck and across both collarbones, nowhere lower, never reaching her chest — never jagged, never zigzag, a clean straight cut like a cross-section. Real skin above this straight line, the material immediately below it. At that line, the material's edge rises in a small raised step above her flesh, casting a crisp shadow.

Her whole body below the collarbones is divided into four irregular rectangular panels of clearly different sizes — not a simple even grid, but panels of different widths and heights, like an asymmetric abstract painting — separated by thick, matte-black dividing bands. A large panel covering most of her left arm and the upper-left of her chest: solid transparent crystal, solid golden-yellow citrine crystal, with faint feathery inclusions and colour zoning, deep honey-gold where thickest and pale lemon at every thin edge. A narrow panel down her right arm only: carved genuine turquoise, a vivid sky-blue to blue-green stone laced with fine dark matrix veining, polished to a smooth, cool sheen, completely opaque, completely opaque. A small square panel at the centre of her belly: a sculpted vessel of clear glass (unmistakably glass, crystal-clear and polished, bright specular reflections) filled with clear rose-pink water holding a scattered handful of deep red rose petals drifting slowly. A large panel covering her hips and both thigh-stubs: carved dark wenge wood, a deep near-black wood finely striped with narrow gold-tan pinstripes, polished to a hard satin sheen, completely opaque, completely opaque, satin-finished at both tips. At every seam where two different materials meet, one material's edge rises very slightly above its neighbour, catching a thin, crisp shadow line — this tiny physical step, repeated at every single boundary in this pattern, is what proves each piece is a truly separate object, not a flat pattern painted onto one continuous surface. At the thick black bands specifically, this step is more pronounced than elsewhere, giving each panel a slightly raised, inset appearance, like tiles set into a frame.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a deep crimson red on one side and a bright cobalt blue on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, her left hand (crystal) resting on her flared hip, her right arm held clear of her body, the hand relaxed at hip height, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: two large softboxes rake across her body from either side, so red light glances off one side and blue light glances off the other, catching a crisp glint of shadow along every stepped seam, light passing straight through the crystal and vessel panels while only reflecting off the stone and wood panels. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
